text:
Edmonton arrives off a 4-0 win over Calgary, the game that ended the Flames' four-game winning streak, with Tristan Jarry stopping all 24 shots. The Oilers are 3-1-1 in their last five and still without Zach Hyman (neck); Colton Dach has stepped into his spot beside Kapanen and Nugent-Hopkins and is up to 16:50 a night from 13:16. The Islanders are also 3-1-1 over five, and Matthew Schaefer won it in overtime at Minnesota on Thursday. They're missing Matias Maccelli and Calum Ritchie, and Simon Holmstrom has taken on more power-play and even-strength time.

The numbers say two evenly matched teams. Both have taken about half the expected goals (the quality of shots created) at five on five, and our model has EDM at 3.07 goals tonight to NYI's 2.88. The special-teams matchup is the one to watch: Edmonton's power play creates 0.89 expected goals a game against an Islanders penalty kill that allows 0.88, and New York takes 4.4 penalties a game. In net, projected starter Jarry sits at -4.3 goals saved above expected (how many goals he's kept out compared with an average goalie facing the same shots), while Ilya Sorokin is at +5.9 this season and +22.3 last.

Connor McDavid, on a 13-game point streak, is 92% for a point in our numbers. Bo Horvat tops the Islanders at 40% to score. Our under-the-radar pick is Holmstrom, 47% for a point, above what his season pace says, because his ice time is up (20:08 a night projected, 18:12 on the season).
